title: Stage 1 semantic roles
description: The contract between Stage 1 (interpret) and Stage 2 (map). Deliberately free of ECS vocabulary: Stage 1 must describe what a field MEANS without being able to name where it goes. If an ECS field name appears here, the decomposition has collapsed and the two stages are no longer separately trainable.

format_summary.description: How the line is structured, in plain language, NAMING any delimiter rather than its family - 'key=value pairs separated by ", "' rather than 'comma-separated'. REQUIRED: Stage 2 chooses extraction.kind from this and nothing else, and has to reproduce the separator exactly without ever seeing a line. Left out, it guesses - it once chose csv for a key=value source and invented a column name to fill the list.

role.description: Plain-language semantic role, e.g. 'address the connection came from'. Never an ECS field name.

value_semantics.description: What the VALUES mean, e.g. 'denied means the attempt was rejected'. Drives value_maps in Stage 2.

unit.description: Unit of measure when the value is numeric, e.g. 'seconds', 'bytes'. Stage 2 cannot detect a unit mismatch it was never told about.

evidence.description: documentation:<anchor> | sample:<n> | inference. A role backed by 'inference' is weaker and the repair loop is allowed to say so.

value_shape.description: What the values LOOK LIKE, in words, when the shape decides between two ECS fields - e.g. 'a bare command name, not an absolute path', 'a short hostname, not an FQDN', 'a numeric identifier, not a display name'. Describe the shape; never quote a value. Stage 2 never sees a log line and cannot tell a name from a path it was never shown. This is the sibling of `unit`, which does the same job for numbers.

unresolved.description: A measured outcome, not an error path. Declining a genuinely ambiguous field is correct behaviour and is scored as such.

column_order.description: Source keys in the order they appear on the line. REQUIRED when the layout is delimited, because Stage 2 never sees a log line and cannot recover the order any other way. Omit it for json and key=value layouts, where position carries no meaning.

extraction.description: HOW TO SPLIT THE LINE, decided by the component that can see one. Stage 2 never sees a log line, so it cannot write this and used to reconstruct it from format_summary in prose. That works for a delimiter and fails completely for grok, whose pattern is a literal transcription of the line's shape: the two-stage arms were therefore structurally incapable of parsing free text, and three of the eight evaluation sources are free text. Stage 1 states it here instead. This leaks no ECS vocabulary - delimiters and capture names are not field names - so the blindness that matters is preserved.

kind.description: json: the whole line is a JSON object. kv: repeated key<value_split>value pairs. csv: positional columns, any single separator. grok: anything else - prose with values embedded in it. A line with no value_split character in it is NOT kv.

field_split.description: What separates one field from the next: a LITERAL string, not a regular expression. Write | for a pipe, never \|; nothing here is matched as a pattern, so nothing is escaped. For a tab, write the ordinary JSON escape \t, which decodes to one tab character - not \\t, which decodes to a backslash followed by a t and matches nothing. Required for kv and for csv, including when the separator is a comma. Omit for json and grok.

value_split.description: kv only: what separates a key from its value, usually =. A LITERAL string, on the same terms as field_split.

columns.description: csv only, REQUIRED there: every column left to right, including ones you do not intend to map. A name you choose is fine; position is what matters.

pattern.description: grok only, REQUIRED there. Name each capture with %{SYNTAX:name}; those names become the source keys the next component maps. Match the WHOLE line. You are the only component that will ever see one.

alternatives.description: grok only. Further patterns, one per DIFFERENT KIND of line - 'job N started by X' beside 'node aborted job N owned by X'. Tried in order after `pattern`; the first that matches a line wins. Use the same capture name for the same value in every pattern. A segment that is merely sometimes absent belongs in `pattern` as (?:...)?, not here.

inner.description: json only. A grok over the TEXT of one JSON key, for a JSON line whose values sit inside a message string: {"msg": "Login failed for user ana from 10.0.0.1"}. The json extraction keeps `msg` whole, so no key holds `ana` or `10.0.0.1`; `inner` reads them. `source` names the key (a dotted path for a nested key: log.message). `pattern` and `alternatives` work as for grok, on that key's text, and their capture names become keys beside the JSON keys. Omit when every value already has its own JSON key.

source.description: The JSON key whose text the grok reads, e.g. msg.

pattern.description: A grok over that key's text, matching ALL of it.

alternatives.description: Further patterns for texts that are a DIFFERENT KIND of message.
